issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Farm.singFarmSongVerse: The UML in the problem statement declares a private helper singFarmSongVerse that accepts an Animal (listed in the Farm class members). The template implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares the method as private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) (no formal parameter) at the method signature, while the reference solution declares private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This prevents the template from being implemented to match the UML/solution calling pattern (singFarmSong should call singFarmSongVerse(animal)) and is likely to confuse students about the intended signature and how to use the helper method.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template method signature so it matches the UML and solution. Change the template signature from private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and update the method body to use the passed-in animal (e.g., animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed()). Ensure singFarmSong() iterates animals and calls singFarmSongVerse(animal).

issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for concrete animal classes: The problem statement (UML) and the template Main refer to concrete classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat. The provided reference implementation instead defines classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (with their implementations) while Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java in the solution repository are empty. This divergence in class identifiers breaks the direct mapping between the exercise description/template and the reference code and will confuse students about which classes to implement and which names the tests or examples expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Align class names between artifacts. Option A (recommended): Rename SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat in the solution to Seal/Pig/Goat so the reference implementation matches the UML and template. Option B: Add small adapter classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat in the solution that extend the corresponding Space* classes (e.g., public class Seal extends SpaceSeal { public Seal(String name){ super(name);} }) so both naming conventions work. Option C: If Space-prefixed names are intentional, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to use SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat and document the naming choice. Ensure tests and examples reference the same class identifiers.
